title: FLEXPROF: Flexible, Side-Channel-Free Memory Access
problem: Secure memory controllers that prevent microarchitectural side-channels by allocating fixed 'turns' to co-scheduled VMs impose a ~2x performance slowdown because the schedule must conservatively handle worst-case mixed read/write patterns, leaving memory bus utilization inefficient.
motivation: Eliminating timing-based memory side-channels in shared cloud systems is essential for VM isolation, but the current overhead of 2x slowdown makes secure scheduling impractical for production workloads.
method: FlexProf introduces two types of memory controller turns: read-optimized turns and write-optimized turns, selected via coarse-grain application profiling that observes the read/write ratio without leaking sensitive information. Each turn type is sized and structured for its dominant operation. Flexibility is added so that a read-optimized turn can opportunistically issue writes when read slots are idle (and vice versa), improving utilization while preserving the fixed-turn structure needed to prevent timing side-channels between VMs.
key_novelty: Differentiating memory controller scheduling turns into read-optimized and write-optimized types, determined by side-channel-free coarse profiling, to recover throughput lost by worst-case-only secure scheduling.
contributions: Read-optimized and write-optimized turn types for the secure memory controller, matched to application access patterns via coarse profiling.
Opportunistic cross-turn operation issuance (reads in write turns, writes in read turns) that preserves isolation guarantees while improving utilization.
Up to 33% performance improvement (geometric mean 8%) over state-of-the-art secure memory scheduling on mixed workloads.

metrics.speedup: up to 33% improvement, geometric mean 8% over state-of-the-art
metrics.other: over half of memory-intensive programs show >10% gain

limitations: Hardware implementation complexity and the profiling mechanism's ability to handle dynamically varying workloads are not discussed.
primary_theme: Read/write-differentiated turn scheduling for side-channel-free memory controllers
